verdict.line: You lose extended ranged exchanges before level 6 while Jayce free-pokes from Cannon stance, but you win from level 6 onward by pulling him into melee with E and banishing him 1v1 with R.

brief.thesis: Jayce's entire threat lives in Cannon stance at range — Shock Blast poke, Acceleration Gate speed, Hyper Charge attack speed — while Mordekaiser's only way to close that gap is Death's Grasp's 700-range pull. That structural gap favors Jayce pre-6 and flips hard once Mordekaiser can isolate him with R, which lines up with the measured 51.3% Mordekaiser win rate over 1,424 games, Mordekaiser's solo-kill edge, and OP.GG's own read that this is an aggressive lane once you commit at level 6.

theirWindow.when: Jayce in Cannon stance, Q and E up
theirWindow.what: He can fire Shock Blast and increase its range/damage by sending it through his own Acceleration Gate (E). Don't trade autos into this; hold behind minions and let him spend mana on a poke that isn't followed by a kill threat. OP.GG's own data is explicit: do not fight him while your W (Indestructible) is on cooldown.

yourWindow.when: Level 6+, Jayce forced into melee range
yourWindow.what: Land E (Death's Grasp, 700 range) to drag him in, then immediately R (Realm of Death) to banish him 1v1 away from minions, allies, and his Acceleration Gate. Once he's trapped at point-blank for the duration, his kiting tools stop mattering and the fight becomes a straight stat race you're built to win.

start.why: Measured 54.2% win rate over 688 games, the higher of the two listed starts in this matchup, and it keeps you solvent through the mana-hungry early trades where you're mostly absorbing poke rather than returning it.

boots.why: 84.5% pick rate and 50.7% win rate — Jayce's damage before and after his stance swap is heavily auto-attack based, and Steelcaps directly cuts that.

core.why: The slow from your Q and E is what actually keeps Jayce from walking back to max range after you pull him in with E.
Sustained damage and omnivamp win the extended skirmish you create once R has isolated him — this exact path hits 59.2% over 103 games.
Burn damage punishes him for sitting inside your E/R zone and stacks cleanly with the Rylai's slow.

situational.when: you need an extra gap-closer to punish his cannon-stance poke before level 6
he starts building into crit or heavy sustained auto-attack damage
you need more mobility and CC utility to actually land E on him
you need a defensive active against burst once teamfights start

runes.keystoneWhy: Ramps during the extended melee skirmish you force after E-into-R, and the adaptive force/omnivamp from stacking it turns a close-quarters fight into sustained healing while he has no range to disengage.

summoners.why: The most picked and highest-sample combo (52.1% win, 65.3% pick) — Mordekaiser holds the solo-kill edge in this matchup, and Ignite is what converts an E-into-R isolation into an actual kill instead of a trade.

playing.title: Hold trades until level 6
playing.detail: Before 6 you have no reliable way to close distance beyond E's 700-range pull. Eat Cannon-stance poke behind minions and prioritize farming over short trades.

playing.title: Watch for the stance swap
playing.detail: R instantly swaps Jayce between Hammer and Cannon on a 6s cooldown, and his first attack after swapping is empowered — armor/MR shred coming out of Hammer, bonus magic damage coming out of Cannon. The stance icon changing is your warning that a trade is about to start.

playing.title: Pull with E before anything else
playing.detail: Death's Grasp is your only tool that drags him out of kiting range. Land it first so he can't walk the fight back to max range before your Q lands.

playing.title: Chain R off a landed E
playing.detail: Realm of Death isolates him 1v1 away from his Acceleration Gate and allies, stripping the positioning tools he needs to kite. Use it the instant E connects for a clean all-in.

playing.title: Never engage with W down
playing.detail: Jayce's full gated Shock Blast combo punishes you hard if Indestructible is on cooldown. Disengage and let it reset before re-initiating.

playing.title: Bank damage, pop the heal late
playing.detail: Let W store incoming Shock Blast and auto damage during poke exchanges, then consume it for the heal right before you commit to your all-in window.

playing.title: Repeat the pattern, don't split
playing.detail: You hold the solo-kill edge here — once you isolate him once, look to repeat E-into-R on cooldown (140/120/100/90/80s) rather than giving him space to re-establish range.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, rune pages, summoner picks, and every win rate above are pulled from measured Mordekaiser vs Jayce games on the current patch via OP.GG; the timing windows, stance-tracking advice, and trade patterns are my own tactical read of the ability kits, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Do not fight Jayce when your [W] is on cooldown. Try to fight him in close quarters after reaching level 6 to gain lane control.
